decision_conditions: The development hereby permitted shall not be carried out otherwise than in complete accordance with the approved plans (as set out on page one of this decision notice).
For the avoidance of doubt and to ensure that the development is carried out as approved.

Unless within two months of the date of this decision, a Noise Management Plan is submitted in writing to the Local Planning Authority for approval, to address concerns regarding possible noise from the hereby permitted change of use and unless the approved scheme is implemented within 1 month of the Local Planning Authority's approval, the use of the site for supported living shall cease until such time as a scheme is approved and implemented. The use shall be operated in accordance with the approved Noise Management Plan. Any modifications to the Noise Management Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.  The Noise Management Plan shall be adhered to at all times whilst the permitted use continues.
Reason: To protect the residential amenities of adjoining properties from noise.

If no scheme in accordance with condition 2 above is approved within four months of the date of this decision notice, the use of the site for supported living shall cease until such time as a scheme is approved by the Local Planning Authority and is implemented.
Reason:-To protect the residential amenities of adjoining properties from noise.

Within two months of the date of this decision notice, the refuse and recycling stores shall be provided in accordance with Drawing No.'s 25-040-002 Rev A and 25-040-160 and be permanently retained thereafter.
Reason: To protect the amenity of occupiers of the development and also the locality generally.
Within two months of the date of this decision notice, the cycle store shall be provided in accordance with Drawing No.'s 25-040-002 Rev A and 25-040-160 and be permanently retained thereafter.
Reason: In the interests of providing a wide range of facilities for non-motor car residents and sustainability.

The maximum number of residents occupying the premises hereby approved shall not exceed four at any one time disregarding staff. There shall be a maximum of two staff unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: To restrict the use of the premises to one compatible with the surrounding area and that the development accords with Policy 16 of the Havering Local Plan 2016-2031.

Statement Required by Article 35 (2) of the Town and Country Planning (Development Management Procedure) (England) Order 2015: In accordance with paragraph 38 of the National Planning Policy Framework, improvements required to make the proposal acceptable were negotiated with CHP Architecture Ltd via email on 26th March, 25th August, 3rd, 10th and 16th September 2026 and on the telephone on 17th September 2026. The revisions involved revising the Planning Statement, relocating the cycle and refuse/recycling stores and amending the plans and the description of the proposal to include a garage conversion. The amendments were subsequently submitted on 10th and 17th September 2026.
description: Retrospective change of use from Use Class C3(a) (dwellinghouse) to supported living for up to 4 people and garage conversion.
